page: OVHcloud d2-4 is a virtual server belonging to the Discovery family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor (Haswell, no TSX) running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, paired with 4.0 GB of memory, which equates to 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 50 GB NVMe SSD. The network configuration lists a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both rank in the bottom 10%, with scores of 932.77 and 1818.26 respectively. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 19.19 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 14.22 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show limited throughput, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 544.76 and single-threaded gzip compression at 14.62 GB/sec. For database operations, the server achieves 2.07 million operations per second on Redis SET tests, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 1.89 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and entry-level hardware specifications, this server offers a low-cost entry point suitable for non-production environments. The trade-off for its affordability is constrained processing power and memory bandwidth, as evidenced by its bottom-tier benchmark rankings. It is best suited for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads such as basic web serving, development sandboxes, small-scale testing, or simple utility scripts that do not require sustained high-performance compute or high network throughput.
